prompts.title: Recent Form — Kinetic Slabs, Honest Data Slate
prompts.prompt: 9:16 vertical, 8 seconds, one sequence containing both named variants. EDITORIAL VARIANT — 'Forma reciente': full-bleed charcoal #101412 with a slow drifting lime #c5ed74 grain. The two Spanish team names of the fixture enter as heavy condensed uppercase slabs in warm white #edf0e6, each snapping down with a hard cut and a low impact pulse, then sliding apart to the left and right edges, leaving a narrow vertical gutter in the centre. Inside the gutter a rhythmic ladder of generic form ticks — small squares, no numerals, no results, no invented streaks — pulses in sync with the spoken cadence; each tick flares lime on a stressed syllable and settles back to slate #8ca6bf. Accent words lifted from the narration float behind the slabs as oversized blurred ghost type, drifting upward, never legible enough to assert a quantity. Camera: slow four-point push in, then a lateral whip right on the final beat. Single focal point: the gutter. transition: a lime wipe travelling bottom to top bridges into the second variant. Exit: both slabs compress into one bar and fade to charcoal. EDITORIAL carries no axes, no source claims, no sample claims and no invented match events. STATISTICAL VARIANT — honest unavailable sequence: because no verified form facts exist for this fixture, the scene resolves into a centred Spanish title 'Datos no disponibles' in warm white on charcoal, a thin slate rule beneath it, and restrained geometric animation — three slim rectangles sliding into alignment and holding still. No axes, no zero line, no counts, no proportions, no invented values. A discreet Spanish line states that no verified sample is available for this fixture, and the source field remains a neutral 'sin fuente verificada' label rather than a fabricated attribution. Camera holds static so the message reads as calm and trustworthy. transition out: the slate rule extends and becomes the baseline of the following scene. The lower quarter of the 9:16 frame is permanently reserved for yellow Spanish subtitles, and every element sits above that band in a clean hierarchy.

prompts.title: Head to Head — Visual Duel, No Inventory of Results
prompts.prompt: 9:16 vertical, 7 seconds, two named variants in a single sequence. EDITORIAL VARIANT — 'Duelo': the frame splits into two mirrored vertical halves on charcoal #101412. The Spanish home team name grows from the left edge in warm white #edf0e6; the Spanish away team name grows from the right edge in slate #8ca6bf. Both are set in the same condensed uppercase face at the same optical size so neither side dominates. A lime #c5ed74 seam of light runs down the centre and vibrates faintly, tightening with each stressed word of the narration. On the emphasised beat the two halves push inward, shoulders colliding at the seam, then recoil to their original positions; particles of warm white scatter and dissolve. A short generic Spanish heading such as 'Cara a cara' or a phrase taken directly from the narration sits small and centred across the seam. No scorelines, no historical tallies, no invented encounters, no timeline of matches. Camera: locked, with a subtle parallax as the halves separate. transition: the lime seam flares and swallows the frame, becoming the next scene's background. Exit: both halves collapse toward the centre line and fade. STATISTICAL VARIANT — honest unavailable sequence: no historical head-to-head counts are published in the catalog, so the scene becomes a quiet Spanish title card reading 'Datos no disponibles' in warm white, centred, above a slender slate rule. Two blank outlined panels sit either side, mirrored but empty — outlines only, never axes, never zeros, never tallies — and a small Spanish caption notes that the historical sample is not available here, with the source line left as a neutral placeholder rather than an invented attribution. Motion is restrained: the outlines fade in offset by a single beat, and the rule draws itself left to right. Camera remains static. transition out: the centre seam of the following scene inherits the lime edge. The lower quarter of the 9:16 frame stays permanently reserved for yellow Spanish subtitles, untouched by any graphic.
